package_info.package_name: Unknown (multiple typosquatting packages, name not specified)
package_info.package_versions: All versions uploaded between March 27 and March 28, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain obfuscated, encrypted malicious code in setup.py that executes automatically upon installation, downloads and decrypts a second-stage payload, steals sensitive data (including crypto wallets and browser data), and establishes persistence. The entire package is designed for credential and data theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code in setup.py decrypts and executes an encrypted payload using Fernet, enabling execution of further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py is used to execute obfuscated, encrypted code at install time, which is not standard for legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only contain standard installation logic, not arbitrary encrypted code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption may be used for protecting proprietary logic, but not in setup.py and not for code that executes automatically.
key_indicators: Use of Fernet decryption at install time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code constructs a URL with the package name and downloads a second-stage payload from a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py is used to fetch code from an external server, which is not expected during package installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should not perform network requests to download and execute additional code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may download dependencies, but not arbitrary encrypted payloads.
key_indicators: Dynamic URL construction with package name

execution_context.file_location: Decrypted second-stage payload (in-memory or dropped file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the decrypted payload harvests sensitive data (crypto wallets, browser data, credentials) and exfiltrates it to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating sensitive user data is a hallmark of info-stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or transmit user credentials or browser data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may scan for credentials with user consent, but not exfiltrate them.
key_indicators: Access to browser and wallet data

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: # Persistence mechanism (e.g., registry modification, autorun script creation)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the payload establishes persistence to survive system reboots, ensuring continued malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence mechanisms are commonly used by malware to maintain access after reboots.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not modify system startup or persistence settings.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management tools may set up persistence with user consent.
key_indicators: Modification of autorun or startup settings
Persistence logic in a package installation context

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious package, triggering setup.py execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decryption and execution of embedded malicious code.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py downloads a second-stage payload from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the downloaded, encrypted payload.

attack_chain.action: Second-stage payload is decrypted and executed, harvesting sensitive data (crypto wallets, browser data, credentials).
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of stolen data to attacker-controlled server.

attack_chain.action: Payload establishes persistence to survive system reboots.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continued malicious activity and data theft after reboot.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py containing obfuscated or encrypted code
setup.py making network requests to download additional payloads
Decryption and execution of code at install time
Harvesting and exfiltration of sensitive data (wallets, browser data, credentials)
Persistence mechanism creation during package installation
file_indicators: setup.py containing base64-encoded or encrypted blobs
Temporary files or scripts created for persistence
network_indicators: Connections to funcaptcha.ru or similar suspicious domains
Dynamic URL construction with package name as parameter
Outbound traffic during or immediately after package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for setup.py files in PyPI packages that contain encrypted or obfuscated code, especially those using Fernet or base64 decoding. Flag packages that make network requests to download additional payloads during installation. Detect access to sensitive files (browser data, crypto wallets) and attempts to establish persistence. Monitor for outbound connections to known malicious domains such as funcaptcha.ru.
